action: Barracuda Managed XDR Cloud or Monitored Endpoint customers who were contacted: revoke and recreate API integration credentials. Everyone: retire long-lived keys held by third parties, use short-lived scoped credentials, and rehearse rotating secrets at scale.
exec: A forgotten key held by a supplier let an automated attacker into a security vendor; some XDR customers were asked to reissue credentials.
plain: Barracuda says an old access key it had left with an outside AI supplier was used to get into about 10 of its cloud accounts for under two days in early November, using an automated AI attack tool.

key_findings: The attacker used a cloud access key Barracuda had issued to a third-party AI vendor for a past project and never retired; the vendor's development environment was compromised in October.
Activity ran from November 1 04:33 UTC to November 2 23:31 UTC and touched about 10 cloud accounts; it was noticed on November 4 after it had stopped.
The attacker hunted secrets, infrastructure state files and Kubernetes credentials, deployed a container mounting the host filesystem, and was blocked from creating a new admin identity.
One reachable system held credentials Barracuda XDR uses to collect customer data; no direct evidence of access was found but logging could not rule it out.
Barracuda attributes the method, not the actor, to the open-source ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework.
recommendations: Remove standing credentials, especially long-lived keys held by third parties; use short-lived, narrowly scoped ones.
Limit blast radius so no single credential opens the next system.
Assume compromise and be able to rotate secrets at scale and rebuild from known-good states.
Customers contacted by Barracuda should revoke and recreate Managed XDR API integration credentials.

summary: Barracuda's CISO says an attacker used a cloud access key the company had given a third-party AI vendor for a past project and never retired. From November 1 to 2 the attacker touched about 10 cloud accounts, harvested secrets and planted a container in a Kubernetes cluster. Activity matched the ARTEX framework. Barracuda rotated all reachable credentials and asked some Managed XDR customers to recreate integration credentials.
title: Barracuda links breach of its cloud accounts to ARTEX AI attack framework
